endorsements.quote: Ensure physicians maintain agency and ultimate decision-making authority, irrespective of generative AI recommendations.
Seek to address bias in generative AI performance through more representative training data, evaluation and mitigation of bias in outputs, and ongoing monitoring of performance.

Seek to understand the perspectives of patients and community organizations when assessing the equity impact of generative as these stakeholders are often able to surface important concerns early in the adoption process.
Demand diverse training data sets, transparency into performance, and equitable outcomes in order to promote fairness when using generative AI.
Ensure strong internal infrastructure is in place to monitor performance of generative AI, especially in clinical use.
Critically evaluate data on generative AI performance when making adoption decisions, recognizing that industry may have different incentives than healthcare organizations.

unlisted_practices: Technologists should design generative AI tools that provide obvious and intuitive mechanisms for verification and error-proofing.
Technologists should hold generative AI tools to the performance standards expected of the clinical workforce rather than expecting clinicians to supervise them.
Technologists should fund high-quality clinical trials and real-world outcomes evaluations of generative AI performance.
Clinicians should not use generative AI tools to make clinical decisions unless confident they can justify those decisions to patients and peers.
Clinicians should insist on high standards of transparency and evidence for AI tools, including potential for bias.
Technologists should create internal systems of checks and balances to manage tensions between business and healthcare ethical standards.
Technologists should co-design generative AI solutions with clinicians and patients.
Healthcare organizations should resist substituting the human workforce with generative AI.
Healthcare organizations should avoid layering generative AI on top of dysfunctional or burdensome workflows and should reimagine workflows instead.
Healthcare organizations should direct resources toward both incremental and transformational generative AI change.
Healthcare organizations should partner with physicians to understand the acceptability of new generative AI-driven workflows and responsibilities.

screen.reason: This is a position statement and consensus recommendation document from the Society of General Internal Medicine regarding the use and governance of generative AI in medicine.
